title: Quarterly paid-media review from the raw daily export
prompt:
You are the retained marketing analyst for Verra Threads, a DTC apparel brand. The CMO has asked for the quarterly paid-media performance review. The complete daily ads export for the last 14 weeks (2026-03-02 through 2026-06-07) is supplied below as CSV; every figure you need is in it, and nothing outside it may be cited as data.

Write the review the CMO will actually read: what is working, what is broken, and what you would change next week, grounded in numbers you computed from the export. Show enough method that a colleague could re-derive any figure you cite.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Net conversions = conversions - refunded_conversions. Net revenue = revenue_usd - refunded_revenue_usd.
- An adset-day is one CSV row. Wasted spend = total spend_usd across adset-days with conversions = 0.
- Weeks are Monday-start calendar weeks: W1 = 2026-03-02 through 2026-03-08, W2 starts 2026-03-09, and so on through W14 = 2026-06-01 through 2026-06-07.
- The final 28 days = 2026-05-11 through 2026-06-07 inclusive.

End the review with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer, each line starting with the label:

A1: <blended CPA across the full 14 weeks: total spend divided by net conversions, in dollars>
A2: <total wasted spend across the full 14 weeks, in dollars>
A3: <the week number, 1-14, in which the prospecting-broad campaign's weekly net ROAS (net revenue divided by spend) first fell below 1.0>
A4: <total refunded revenue of the single adset with the most refunded revenue, in dollars>
A5: <account-wide net ROAS for the final 28 days, to two decimals>

This is an internal analysis for review only. Do not fetch external data and do not invent benchmarks.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all five labeled answers A1-A5 are present and parseable.
A1 states the blended CPA (total spend / net conversions) for the full 14 weeks; full credit within 0.5% of the value computed from the export, zero credit beyond 10% off.
A2 states total spend across zero-conversion adset-days; full credit within 1%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A3 names the week (1-14) in which prospecting-broad's weekly net ROAS first fell below 1.0; full credit for the exact week, partial credit within one week, zero credit two or more weeks off.
A4 states the total refunded revenue of the adset with the most refunded revenue; full credit within 1%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A5 states the account-wide net ROAS for the final 28 days; full credit within 1%, zero credit beyond 15% off.

skill_adherence.check: The analysis states that conversions and revenue were computed net of refunds (or shows the refund adjustment explicitly) rather than silently using gross figures.
The review names rt-lookalike as the adset with the largest refunded revenue.

Every figure presented as an observed or computed fact anywhere in the review is derivable from the recorded CSV for the named segment, dates and units. Inspect tables, notes and the action plan independently of the A1-A5 block. Check decision-relevant starting amounts against source totals; citing an adset name and a number is not verification. Do not invent numerical costs, configured budgets, attribution rates or segment measurements. Explicitly labeled future proposals and hypotheses are not historical figures. Assess causal interpretations and recommendation feasibility separately under recommendation_grounded.

best_practices.check: The review identifies prospecting-broad's performance decline across the window as a trend requiring action, not merely a low average.

The review specifically calls out the pb-video adset as continuing to spend while producing zero conversions in the final weeks (or an equivalent adset-level wasted-spend identification naming pb-video).

Recommendations follow from named campaigns/adsets and verified figures with the relevant period and units. Explicit transfers, cuts and increases reconcile with their stated funding; flag double allocation only when stated amounts or allocations conflict. A transfer based on observed spend cannot exceed that baseline without an explicit additional source or a conditional budget assumption to verify. Observed spend is not configured budget, available scale or profit. Do not require a fully costed budget for qualitative creative, investigation or future rebuild suggestions, or infer a second budget commitment solely because later work may cost money. Causes and future outcomes remain hypotheses unless established by the source.
